new_model.summary: Create an empty model in the workspace under *name*.
new_model.doc: new_model: Create an empty model in the workspace under *name*. Arguments: name: Workspace name for the new model (your handle for it later).

open_model.summary: Load a model file from the workspace root into the workspace.
open_model.doc: open_model: Load a model file from the workspace root into the workspace. Arguments: path: Model .json path, relative to the workspace root.; name: Workspace name to load it under; defaults to the file stem.

import_xmile.summary: Translate an XMILE (Stella/iThink) system-dynamics file into a new model.
import_xmile.doc: import_xmile: Translate an XMILE (Stella/iThink) system-dynamics file into a new model. Arguments: path: XMILE (.xmile/.stmx) file, relative to the workspace root.; name: Workspace name to load it under; defaults to the file stem.

import_mdl.summary: Translate a Vensim system-dynamics file into a new model.
import_mdl.doc: import_mdl: Translate a Vensim system-dynamics file into a new model. Arguments: path: Vensim (.mdl) file, relative to the workspace root.; name: Workspace name to load it under; defaults to the file stem.

import_event_log.summary: Draft a model from an event log: what happened to each case, activity by activity.
import_event_log.doc: import_event_log: Draft a model from an event log: what happened to each case, activity by activity. Arguments: path: Event log (CSV, or .xes), relative to the workspace root.; name: Workspace name to open the draft under; defaults to the file stem.; routing: "auto" (a test on the log picks), "markov" (chances to the next activity) or "variants" (one routing per observed sequence).; time_unit: The draft's time unit: seconds, minutes, hours or days. A numeric timestamp is taken as already in it.; idle_waits: true: each activity that waits long at mostly idle resources gets a DELAY before it, fitted to its waits (a modelled wait, not a queue); false (default): no such delay.

save_model.summary: Write a model in the workspace to disk as JSON.
save_model.doc: save_model: Write a model in the workspace to disk as JSON. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to save.; path: Destination path under the workspace root; defaults to where it was opened.

list_models.summary: List the models currently open in the workspace, and the model files available under the workspace root.
list_models.doc: list_models: List the models currently open in the workspace, and the model files available under the workspace root.

get_model_summary.summary: A compact picture of a model: its blocks with their key parameters, its links in branch order, its resources, and how many problems it has.
get_model_summary.doc: get_model_summary: A compact picture of a model: its blocks with their key parameters, its links in branch order, its resources, and how many problems it has. Arguments: model:

get_model_json.summary: The complete model layout as the JSON that would be saved to disk.
get_model_json.doc: get_model_json: The complete model layout as the JSON that would be saved to disk. Arguments: model:

undo.summary: Undo the last edit to a model.
undo.doc: undo: Undo the last edit to a model. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.

redo.doc: redo: Redo the edit that `undo` reversed. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.

add_block.summary: Add one block to a model and optionally set its parameters in the same step (one undo entry).
add_block.doc: add_block: Add one block to a model and optionally set its parameters in the same step (one undo entry). Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; type: Block type, e.g. "CREATE", "PROCESS", "DISPOSE" (see list_block_types).; name: Block name; auto-generated (create_1, process_2, ...) when omitted.; params: Parameter values to set on the block; the type's defaults fill the rest.; position: [x, y] canvas centre in scene units; auto-placed in a row when omitted.

update_block.summary: Change an existing block: merge parameters, rename it, move it, or relabel it -- all as one undo entry.
update_block.doc: update_block: Change an existing block: merge parameters, rename it, move it, or relabel it -- all as one undo entry. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; name: Current name of the block to change.; params: Parameters to merge into the block's existing params.; description: New canvas label.; position: New [x, y] centre.; new_name: Rename the block to this; every link follows the rename.

remove_blocks.summary: Delete blocks and every link touching them, as one undo entry.
remove_blocks.doc: remove_blocks: Delete blocks and every link touching them, as one undo entry. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; names: Block names to delete; their links go with them.

connect.summary: Link two blocks so entities flow from *source* to *target*, optionally with a transfer delay.
connect.doc: connect: Link two blocks so entities flow from *source* to *target*, optionally with a transfer delay. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; source: Name of the block the entity leaves.; target: Name of the block the entity arrives at.; source_port: Out port name, only when the source is a SUBMODEL instance.; target_port: In port name, only when the target is a SUBMODEL instance.; delay: Optional transfer delay, e.g. {"distribution": "Constant", "dist_params": {"value": 2}}.

disconnect.doc: disconnect: Remove one link. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; source: Source block of the link to remove.; target: Target block of the link to remove.; index: Which of several parallel links between the pair, 0 first; only needed when there is more than one.

reorder_branches.summary: Set the branch order of a block's outgoing links.
reorder_branches.doc: reorder_branches: Set the branch order of a block's outgoing links. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; source: The branching block (a DECIDE or LOGIC).; order: Its target block names in the branch order you want, branch 0 first.

set_resources.summary: REPLACE the model's whole resource table.
set_resources.doc: set_resources: REPLACE the model's whole resource table. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; resources: The complete resource list, each {"name", "capacity", "discipline", cost fields...}.

set_calendar.summary: Give the model REAL DATES, or remove them.
set_calendar.doc: set_calendar: Give the model REAL DATES, or remove them. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; start: ISO 8601 instant model time 0 stands for, e.g. "2026-01-05T06:00:00". With no offset it is read in `timezone`, never in local time. Pass null to remove the calendar.; timezone: IANA name such as UTC or Europe/Rome (default UTC). The wall clock weekday schedules and every date label use.; end: Optional ISO instant the run ends at, instead of a run-length number.

set_entity_types.doc: set_entity_types: REPLACE the model's entity-type table. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; entities: The complete entity-type list, each {"name", "shape"?, "color"?, "holding_cost"?}.

set_simulation_settings.summary: Set the model's default run settings; only the arguments you pass change.
set_simulation_settings.doc: set_simulation_settings: Set the model's default run settings; only the arguments you pass change. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; run_length: Run length in base time units; 0/null means "until the model drains". With a calendar you can set an end DATE instead, with set_calendar.; warmup: Time at which statistics are reset.; replications: How many independent replications a run does by default.; time_unit: The model's BASE unit: seconds, minutes, hours or days.; currency: Cost label only; never enters the arithmetic.

set_sd_settings.summary: Turn on the system-dynamics step grid, change it, or remove it (dt null).
set_sd_settings.doc: set_sd_settings: Turn on the system-dynamics step grid, change it, or remove it (dt null). Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; dt: Step of the system-dynamics grid, > 0; null removes the grid.; method: euler (Stella/Vensim default) or rk4 (fourth order; no random draws in a dynamic rate).; time_unit: Unit dt is in: base (the model's own) or seconds/minutes/hours/days.

auto_layout.summary: Lay the model's blocks out left to right in a deterministic layered arrangement, one undo entry.
auto_layout.doc: auto_layout: Lay the model's blocks out left to right in a deterministic layered arrangement, one undo entry. Arguments: model:

get_record_schema.summary: The JSON Schema of one record of *section*: what `upsert_record` expects.
get_record_schema.doc: get_record_schema: The JSON Schema of one record of *section*: what `upsert_record` expects. Arguments: section: Record section, e.g. "resources", "tables", "levels", "agent_types", "orders" (get_record_schema lists them all).

list_records.summary: List every record of one section of the model, as stored.
list_records.doc: list_records: List every record of one section of the model, as stored. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; section: Record section, e.g. "resources", "tables", "levels", "agent_types", "orders" (get_record_schema lists them all).

upsert_record.summary: Add a record to a section, or REPLACE the one with the same key.
upsert_record.doc: upsert_record: Add a record to a section, or REPLACE the one with the same key. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; section: Record section, e.g. "resources", "tables", "levels", "agent_types", "orders" (get_record_schema lists them all).; record: The whole record, shaped as get_record_schema(section) says; its key field ("name", or "id" for orders) picks the record to replace.

remove_record.doc: remove_record: Delete one record. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; section: Record section, e.g. "resources", "tables", "levels", "agent_types", "orders" (get_record_schema lists them all).; key: The record's key: its "name" (its "id" for orders).

upsert_table_from_csv.summary: Read a CSV under the workspace root into a lookup table.
upsert_table_from_csv.doc: upsert_table_from_csv: Read a CSV under the workspace root into a lookup table. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; name: Table name to create or replace.; path: CSV file under the workspace root.; key_mode: Lookup mode for the row keys: exact, step or linear.; column_mode: Lookup mode for the column keys.; default: Value for a missing exact key.

list_continuous.summary: List the model's time-series inputs, levels and flows in one answer.
list_continuous.doc: list_continuous: List the model's time-series inputs, levels and flows in one answer. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to inspect.

upsert_timeseries_input_from_csv.summary: Read a `time,value` CSV under the workspace root into a time-series input.
upsert_timeseries_input_from_csv.doc: upsert_timeseries_input_from_csv: Read a `time,value` CSV under the workspace root into a time-series input. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; name: Series name to create or replace.; path: CSV file under the workspace root, two columns: time and value.; interpolation: step or linear.; beyond: hold, repeat or error.; time_unit: Unit the time column is in.

get_network.summary: The model's path network: the nodes assets sit on and the segments vehicles and walkers drive along, with the shortest-path distance between every pair of places.
get_network.doc: get_network: The model's path network: the nodes assets sit on and the segments vehicles and walkers drive along, with the shortest-path distance between every pair of places. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to inspect.

upsert_node.summary: Add a network node, or move the one with this name.
upsert_node.doc: upsert_node: Add a network node, or move the one with this name. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; name: Node name; a STATION's `node` param, a fleet's `home` and DISTANCE("...", ...) all address it by this.; x: Layout x coordinate (metres once the background declares a scale).; y: Layout y coordinate.

remove_node.summary: Delete a network node AND the segments that used it (a segment with a dangling end is not a thing a model can mean).
remove_node.doc: remove_node: Delete a network node AND the segments that used it (a segment with a dangling end is not a thing a model can mean). Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; name: Node to delete; every segment touching it goes with it.

upsert_segment.summary: Add a drivable segment between two nodes, or replace the one already joining that ordered pair.
upsert_segment.doc: upsert_segment: Add a drivable segment between two nodes, or replace the one already joining that ordered pair. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; source: Node the segment starts at.; target: Node it ends at.; length: Length in layout units. Omit for the straight-line distance times the network's length_factor -- set it for a ramp, a curve or a detour.; two_way: False makes it one-way from source to target.; speed: Optional speed LIMIT on this segment. It changes travel TIME; the route chosen is still the shortest by length.; capacity: How many vehicles may be on it at once (zone control); omit for unlimited. Two-way with capacity 1 can deadlock head-on.

remove_segment.doc: remove_segment: Delete one segment. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; source: Node the segment starts at.; target: Node it ends at.

get_distance.summary: Shortest path between two places on the model's network.
get_distance.doc: get_distance: Shortest path between two places on the model's network. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to inspect.; source: A node, a STATION block or a station alias.; target: Where the trip ends, named the same way.

list_sequences.summary: List the model's routing sequences and the stations they visit.
list_sequences.doc: list_sequences: List the model's routing sequences and the stations they visit. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to inspect.

list_orders.summary: List the model's orders: released jobs with a due date.
list_orders.doc: list_orders: List the model's orders: released jobs with a due date. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to inspect.

upsert_orders_from_csv.summary: REPLACE (or extend) the model's orders from a CSV release list.
upsert_orders_from_csv.doc: upsert_orders_from_csv: REPLACE (or extend) the model's orders from a CSV release list. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; path: CSV file to read, inside the workspace root.; replace: True (default) replaces the whole order book; False merges by id.

upsert_scenario.summary: Add or update a named scenario: a set of parameter overrides applied to the base model before a run.
upsert_scenario.doc: upsert_scenario: Add or update a named scenario: a set of parameter overrides applied to the base model before a run. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; name: Scenario name; "Baseline" is implicit and always present.; overrides: [{"path": "resources.Server.capacity", "value": 2}, ...].; description: Free-text note about what this scenario represents.; goal: The question this scenario answers, one sentence (max 500 characters).

run_model.summary: Run a model and return a COMPACT KPI digest -- never the raw frames.
run_model.doc: run_model: Run a model and return a COMPACT KPI digest -- never the raw frames. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to run.; replications: Independent replications; defaults to the model's own setting.; run_length: Run length in base time units; defaults to the model's own setting.; warmup: Warm-up time before statistics start; defaults to the model's own setting.; seed: First replication's seed; replication r uses seed + r.; bind_data: Resolve series:/orders data bindings at run time first (default false), like the UI/CLI's `--bind`. This does NOT write bulk data into the model; it only affects this run.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget; the run stops cleanly and returns what finished.

get_kpi_table.summary: Page through one results frame of the last `run_model` for this model.
get_kpi_table.doc: get_kpi_table: Page through one results frame of the last `run_model` for this model. Arguments: model: Workspace name of a model that has been run.; frame: Which frame: system, resource_summary, entity_summary, user_summary, store_summary, entity_log, resource_log, store_log or timeseries.; offset: Rows to skip.; limit: Rows to return (at most 200).

run_scenarios.summary: Run the model's scenarios and compare them against the baseline with confidence intervals and a significance verdict.
run_scenarios.doc: run_scenarios: Run the model's scenarios and compare them against the baseline with confidence intervals and a significance verdict. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to run.; scenarios: Scenario names to run; omit for all of them plus Baseline.; kpis: KPI keys to report, e.g. ["system/Avg Throughput Time"]; omit for the system KPIs.; replications: Replications per scenario.; run_length: Run length in base time units.; warmup: Warm-up time.; seed: Base seed; with CRN every scenario uses the same seeds.; crn: Common random numbers (default true): pairs the scenarios so the comparison uses the low-variance paired-t interval.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget for the whole sweep.

investment_case.summary: Run the model's scenarios and price each against the baseline: extra capex, saving per year, payback, NPV and ROI over the `investment` section's horizon, with confidence intervals from several replications.
investment_case.doc: investment_case: Run the model's scenarios and price each against the baseline: extra capex, saving per year, payback, NPV and ROI over the `investment` section's horizon, with confidence intervals from several replications. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to run; it needs an `investment` section.; replications: Independent replications (capped at 200, like run_to_precision); defaults to the model's own setting.; seed: First replication's seed; replication r uses seed + r.

run_to_precision.summary: Keep adding replications until one KPI's confidence interval is narrow enough, then report how many it took.
run_to_precision.doc: run_to_precision: Keep adding replications until one KPI's confidence interval is narrow enough, then report how many it took. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to run.; kpi: The KPI key to target, e.g. "system/Avg Throughput Time".; relative: Target half-width as a fraction of the mean (default 0.05 = 5%).; absolute: Target half-width in the KPI's own units; overrides `relative`.; max_replications: Hard cap on replications.; run_length: Run length in base time units.; warmup: Warm-up time.; seed: Base seed.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget.

run_reality_checks.summary: Run the model's Vensim-style reality checks: an input imposed on the model (e.g.
run_reality_checks.doc: run_reality_checks: Run the model's Vensim-style reality checks: an input imposed on the model (e.g. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to run.; run_length: Run length in base time units; defaults to the model's own setting.; warmup: Warm-up time before statistics start; defaults to the model's own setting.; seed: Seed shared by every check's deterministic run (CRN across checks).; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget for the whole set of checks.

run_loop_dominance.summary: Which feedback loop drives an SD model's behaviour, and when (Loops That Matter, as in Stella).
run_loop_dominance.doc: run_loop_dominance: Which feedback loop drives an SD model's behaviour, and when (Loops That Matter, as in Stella). Arguments: model: Workspace name of an SD model (needs simulation.sd).; run_length: Run length in base time units; defaults to the model's own setting.; seed: Seed of the one replication the analysis runs.; top: How many loops to return, strongest mean relative score first.

suggest_warmup.summary: Estimate how much of the run to discard as warm-up, using MSER-5 on the throughput-time series.
suggest_warmup.doc: suggest_warmup: Estimate how much of the run to discard as warm-up, using MSER-5 on the throughput-time series. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; replications: Replications to run for the estimate.; run_length: Run length in base time units.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget.

optimize.summary: Search model parameters for the best value of one KPI within a replication budget, then confirm the winner statistically.
optimize.doc: optimize: Search model parameters for the best value of one KPI within a replication budget, then confirm the winner statistically. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; factors: [{"path": "resources.Server.capacity", "kind": "integer", "low": 1, "high": 5}], kind is continuous/integer/categorical.; response: KPI key to optimise, e.g. "system/Avg Throughput Time".; goal: "min" or "max".; constraints: [["<kpi key>", "<=", value], ...] KPI constraints.; budget: Total replications the search may spend.; replications_per_point: Replications per candidate point.; run_length: Run length in base time units.; seed: Base seed.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget.

calibrate.summary: Tune model parameters until the model reproduces measured KPIs.
calibrate.doc: calibrate: Tune model parameters until the model reproduces measured KPIs. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to calibrate.; targets: [{"kpi", "observed", "weight"?, "tolerance"?}] -- the measured values the model must reproduce.; factors: [{"path", "kind", "low", "high"}] -- the parameters to tune.; budget: Total replications the search may spend.; replications_per_point: Replications per candidate point.; seed: Base seed.; apply: Store the fitted values as a "Calibrated" scenario on the model.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget.

forecast.summary: Forecast a short horizon from the model's CURRENT state, with uncertainty bands and event probabilities.
forecast.doc: forecast: Forecast a short horizon from the model's CURRENT state, with uncertainty bands and event probabilities. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to forecast.; horizon: Run length in base time units -- a shift, a day.; replications: Replications; a prediction band needs a few hundred to be stable.; events: [{"name", "kpi", "op": ">"|"<", "value"}] questions to answer as probabilities.; kpis: KPI keys to report; omit for the curated system ones.; bind_data: Resolve the model's data bindings first (default true).; seed: Base seed.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget.

export.summary: Write the last run's results to a file: an Excel workbook, CSV folder, a self-contained HTML report, or JSON.
export.doc: export: Write the last run's results to a file: an Excel workbook, CSV folder, a self-contained HTML report, or JSON. Arguments: model: Workspace name of a model that has been run.; format: Exporter name: xlsx, csv, html, json, or a plugin's own.; path: Destination under the workspace root (a directory for csv).

evaluate_policy.summary: Evaluate a built-in controller against a Policy-mode DECIDE.
evaluate_policy.doc: evaluate_policy: Evaluate a built-in controller against a Policy-mode DECIDE. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; policy: Decision-point name -- must match a Policy-mode DECIDE's `policy` param.; controller: Built-in controller to evaluate: "random", "shortest" or "roundrobin".; episodes: Independent episodes to average over; episode i uses seed + i.; horizon: Episode length in base time units; the episode truncates there if the model has not drained first.; reward: "neg_wip", "throughput", "neg_time_in_system", or an expression string evaluated over model state at each decision (no `entity` in scope).; seed: Base seed.

fit_surrogate.summary: Run a design of experiments and fit a response-surface surrogate over it -- a fast stand-in for the simulation, for optimisation or what-if exploration without spending more replications.
fit_surrogate.doc: fit_surrogate: Run a design of experiments and fit a response-surface surrogate over it -- a fast stand-in for the simulation, for optimisation or what-if exploration without spending more replications. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model.; factors: [{"path": "resources.Server.capacity", "kind": "integer", "low": 1, "high": 5}], same shape as the `optimize` tool's factors.; response: KPI key to fit a surface for, e.g. "system/Avg Throughput Time".; design: full[:levels] (default full:2), lhs:<n>, or oat -- same grammar as `naga doe --design`.; kind: "linear", "quadratic", "auto" (picks by CV RMSE), or -- only if scikit-learn is installed -- "gp"/"forest".; replications: Replications per design point.; run_length: Run length in base time units.; seed: Base seed.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget for the whole design.

resolve_data_bindings.summary: Read the model's data bindings and report what each one produced.
resolve_data_bindings.doc: resolve_data_bindings: Read the model's data bindings and report what each one produced. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to resolve.; apply: Write the resolved values into the model (an undoable edit). False just reports what the bindings WOULD read.

set_initial_state.summary: Give the model a WARM START: work already in the system at t=0.
set_initial_state.doc: set_initial_state: Give the model a WARM START: work already in the system at t=0. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to edit.; entities: [{"block", "count", "e_type"?, "age"?, "in_service"?, "remaining"?, "attributes"?}] -- entities already in each block.; variables: {name: value} the run starts from.; resources: {name: {"down_until": t}} for a resource that starts failed.; time: Timestamp of the snapshot this state came from (recorded, never shifts the clock).

fit_distribution.summary: Fit candidate distributions to observed data and rank them, so a block's duration comes from measurements instead of a guess.
fit_distribution.doc: fit_distribution: Fit candidate distributions to observed data and rank them, so a block's duration comes from measurements instead of a guess. Arguments: path: CSV/TSV/XLSX file under the workspace root holding the sample.; values: An inline list of numbers, instead of a file.; column: Column name in the file; defaults to the first numeric column.; candidates: Distribution families to try; omit for all of them.; top: How many ranked fits to return.

get_plant_timeline.summary: Check a plant mapping against a model and, given a recorded plant log, say what the plant looked like at the log's last instant.
get_plant_timeline.doc: get_plant_timeline: Check a plant mapping against a model and, given a recorded plant log, say what the plant looked like at the log's last instant. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model the mapping is for.; mapping: Plant mapping (*.plantmap.json), a path relative to the workspace root.; log: Recorded plant log (one JSON object a line, as `naga watch --record` writes), a path relative to the workspace root. Empty: only check the mapping.

get_twin_monitor.summary: What the plant looks like now, as the running twin last wrote it.
get_twin_monitor.doc: get_twin_monitor: What the plant looks like now, as the running twin last wrote it.

get_twin_forecast.summary: The running twin's latest forecast, and how its earlier ones compare with what the plant then did.
get_twin_forecast.doc: get_twin_forecast: The running twin's latest forecast, and how its earlier ones compare with what the plant then did.

get_twin_recommendations.summary: What the running twin recommends now, and what became of what it recommended before.
get_twin_recommendations.doc: get_twin_recommendations: What the running twin recommends now, and what became of what it recommended before.

list_block_types.summary: List every block type this build can place in a model, with a one-line summary and its required parameters.
list_block_types.doc: list_block_types: List every block type this build can place in a model, with a one-line summary and its required parameters.

describe_block_type.summary: Describe one block type: what it does and every parameter with its type, default and meaning.
describe_block_type.doc: describe_block_type: Describe one block type: what it does and every parameter with its type, default and meaning. Arguments: type_name: Block type, e.g. "PROCESS".; detail: Every description in full; by default each is its first sentence.

list_distributions.summary: List the distribution names available for a duration or a random draw.
list_distributions.doc: list_distributions: List the distribution names available for a duration or a random draw. Arguments: block_type: Optional block type (e.g. "CREATE", "DELAY") to list only the distributions offered for it; omit for the whole catalogue.

describe_distribution.summary: Describe one distribution: when to use it and what each parameter means.
describe_distribution.doc: describe_distribution: Describe one distribution: when to use it and what each parameter means. Arguments: name:

get_expression_help.summary: Explain the expression language used by ASSIGN, DECIDE/HOLD conditions, RECORD, ranking expressions and expression-valued distribution parameters.
get_expression_help.doc: get_expression_help: Explain the expression language used by ASSIGN, DECIDE/HOLD conditions, RECORD, ranking expressions and expression-valued distribution parameters.

validate_model.summary: Validate a model and return every problem with a stable code, a JSON-pointer path, and a hint saying how to fix it.
validate_model.doc: validate_model: Validate a model and return every problem with a stable code, a JSON-pointer path, and a hint saying how to fix it. Arguments: model:

get_model_format.summary: What a model file holds, compactly: call it ONCE before write_model.
get_model_format.doc: get_model_format: What a model file holds, compactly: call it ONCE before write_model. Arguments: blocks: Block types to describe in full (every parameter with its meaning); omit for the overview.; sections: Model file sections to describe field by field, e.g. ["levels", "schedules"]; omit for the overview.

write_model.summary: Write a WHOLE model in one call: the complete model file as one JSON object.
write_model.doc: write_model: Write a WHOLE model in one call: the complete model file as one JSON object. Arguments: model: Workspace name for the model: a new one is created, an open one replaced.; layout: The complete model file as one JSON object (get_model_format shows its shape): blocks, links, resources, simulation, ...

debug_run.summary: Run one replication of a model under a debugger: start it, or continue it, until a stop, one step, a model time, a pending decision or the end.
debug_run.doc: debug_run: Run one replication of a model under a debugger: start it, or continue it, until a stop, one step, a model time, a pending decision or the end. Arguments: model: Workspace name of the model to debug.; stops: Replaces the stops (a list of at most 50, each text at most 500 characters): [{"block": name}] stops when an entity enters that block (a submodel instance name: anything inside it), [{"entity": id}] when that entity is created or moves, [{"expr": text}] when the expression becomes true. A block or entity stop may add "entity" (that entity only) and "when" (an expression read with the entering entity, e.g. 'entity.e_type == "Red"'). Omit to keep them, [] to clear.; watches: Replaces the watch expressions, read at every return (a list of at most 50 texts of at most 500 characters). Omit to keep, [] to clear.; to: Model time to run to at most (a finite number); omit for no time limit.; step: True: stop at the next event the trace shows (one entity move, one resource change).; decisions: Answers to pending decisions: [{"policy", "option", "request_id"}] (request_id optional: the policy's oldest). Applied after the checks of the other arguments and after a start or `restart`, before the run moves.; restart: True: drop the run and start again from t = 0 on the model as it is now, keeping the stops and watches unless new ones are given.; seed: Seed of the run; read only when the run starts or restarts.; max_seconds: Wall-clock budget for this call; the run stays where it got to. 0 means no budget: the call runs until a stop, `to`, a decision or the end.; back: True: go back to where the previous call left the run, exactly (it is replayed from the seed and the decisions made), and return without moving. The replay runs from t = 0 within max_seconds; when it does not fit, E_BUDGET and the run stays where it was. Not with `to`, `step`, `scope`, `decisions` or `restart`.; scope: With `step`: a submodel instance (or a block); the step goes on to the next event of a block inside it, so it stays where you are looking.

debug_inspect.summary: Read the state of a model's debug run where it stands, without moving it.
debug_inspect.doc: debug_inspect: Read the state of a model's debug run where it stands, without moving it. Arguments: model: Workspace name of a model with a debug run.; block: A block or submodel instance to look into; omit for the overview only.; entity: Id of an entity to read (from a hit, a queue or `pending`).

study_start.summary: Start a simulation study: make its folder and say what to do first.
study_start.doc: study_start: Start a simulation study: make its folder and say what to do first. Arguments: question: The decision or question the study answers, in the person's words.; study: Folder for the study; omit to use naga-studies/<short name of the question>.; mode: one_go (plan approved first, then built) or incremental (built step by step).; size: quick, standard or deep: caps on replications, steps and scenarios.; changes: Keys to record in the same call, with the shapes of study_update's changes.

study_status.summary: Where a study stands, on one screen: sufficiency, goals, the ten-step checklist, the last version's KPIs with how confident they are (precision of the confidence intervals) and the next step.
study_status.doc: study_status: Where a study stands, on one screen: sufficiency, goals, the ten-step checklist, the last version's KPIs with how confident they are (precision of the confidence intervals) and the next step. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).

study_update.summary: Record what the study has learned or the person decided (fewer or more replications: set precision): set any of question, decision, mode, size, plan_approved, precision, goals, target, assumptions, sources, validation, experiments, skipped, inside `changes` or (all but decision) as parameters of the same name (a key sent both ways is refused; decision is changes={"decision": ...} only).
study_update.doc: study_update: Record what the study has learned or the person decided (fewer or more replications: set precision): set any of question, decision, mode, size, plan_approved, precision, goals, target, assumptions, sources, validation, experiments, skipped, inside `changes` or (all but decision) as parameters of the same name (a key sent both ways is refused; decision is changes={"decision": ...} only). Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; changes: Optional if the keys are sent as parameters. Keys to set: question, decision, mode, size, plan_approved, goals, target, assumptions, sources, validation, experiments, skipped. A list key is replaced whole. goals and assumptions entries need a string id; a goal is {id, text, kpi, low, high}; an assumption is {id, text, value, source}; a target component is {name, purpose, blocks: [block names]}; a source is {id, text, input}; a validation entry is {level: data|known_answer|expert, passed: true|false, text}, e.g. {"level": "known_answer", "passed": true, "text": "M/G/1 formula vs model wait"}; an experiment is {id, text, result}.; question: Same as the "question" key of changes.; mode: Same as the "mode" key of changes.; size: Same as the "size" key of changes.; plan_approved: Same as the "plan_approved" key of changes.; precision: Same as the "precision" key of changes.; goals: Same as the "goals" key of changes.; target: Same as the "target" key of changes.; assumptions: Same as the "assumptions" key of changes.; sources: Same as the "sources" key of changes.; validation: Same as the "validation" key of changes.; experiments: Same as the "experiments" key of changes.; skipped: Same as the "skipped" key of changes.

study_add_input.summary: Keep a source of the study in its inputs/ folder: copy a workspace file, or store text (a call transcript, notes).
study_add_input.doc: study_add_input: Keep a source of the study in its inputs/ folder: copy a workspace file, or store text (a call transcript, notes). Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; name: File name to store under inputs/ (no folders).; path: Workspace file to copy in; give this or text.; text: Text to store (a transcript, notes); give this or path.

study_step.summary: Test one model step: write the whole model, run it, check it, and store it as a new version (or as a draft when it fails).
study_step.doc: study_step: Test one model step: write the whole model, run it, check it, and store it as a new version (or as a draft when it fails). Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; layout: The complete model file as one JSON object (as write_model).; note: One line: what changed in this step and why.; request_id: Any unique string; a retried call with the same one is not recorded twice.; seed: First replication's seed.; changes: Keys to record in the same call, with the shapes of study_update's changes. Recorded before the step.

study_validate.summary: Check the last model version against a textbook answer and record the validation.
study_validate.doc: study_validate: Check the last model version against a textbook answer and record the validation. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; kind: The known answer to check against; only queue_formula (M/M/c or M/G/1) exists.

study_accept.summary: Record that the person accepts the study as it stands.
study_accept.doc: study_accept: Record that the person accepts the study as it stands. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; reason: The person's own words accepting the study.

study_revert.summary: Go back to an earlier version: it is recorded again as a new version, so no history is lost.
study_revert.doc: study_revert: Go back to an earlier version: it is recorded again as a new version, so no history is lost. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; version: Id of an earlier version, e.g. v002.; note: Why the study goes back to it.; request_id: Any unique string, as for study_step.

study_report.summary: Write a version's full HTML report (KPIs with intervals, resources, charts) on request.
study_report.doc: study_report: Write a version's full HTML report (KPIs with intervals, resources, charts) on request. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; version: Version id, e.g. v002; omit for the last.

study_package.summary: Build the study's deliverable, the final files to hand over, in its package/ folder: the control room page, an Excel workbook (goals, versions with KPIs, checklist, assumptions), the current model and RO-Crate metadata.
study_package.doc: study_package: Build the study's deliverable, the final files to hand over, in its package/ folder: the control room page, an Excel workbook (goals, versions with KPIs, checklist, assumptions), the current model and RO-Crate metadata. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).

study_view.summary: See a version's flowchart: built blocks, what this step changed and what of the agreed target is not built yet.
study_view.doc: study_view: See a version's flowchart: built blocks, what this step changed and what of the agreed target is not built yet. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; version: Version id, e.g. v002; omit for the last.; format: png (image), svg or text.

study_show.summary: Show the study's control room, its dashboard.
study_show.doc: study_show: Show the study's control room, its dashboard. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).

study_page_html.summary: The control room page as one HTML string.
study_page_html.doc: study_page_html: The control room page as one HTML string. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).

study_sensitivity.summary: Vary one assumption at a time (arrival and service parameters, capacities) around a version, with common random numbers and the version's stored replications and seed, and rank them by how much each moves the goal KPIs.
study_sensitivity.doc: study_sensitivity: Vary one assumption at a time (arrival and service parameters, capacities) around a version, with common random numbers and the version's stored replications and seed, and rank them by how much each moves the goal KPIs. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; version: Version id, e.g. v002; omit for the last.; factors: Paths to vary (as in an earlier answer); omit for the most relevant, at most 8.; delta: Relative change, 0.2 = +-20%; capacities change by +-1.

study_extensions.summary: Candidate extension modules for the study's model: shifts with a break, resource failures (machine breakdowns), an arrival peak.
study_extensions.doc: study_extensions: Candidate extension modules for the study's model: shifts with a break, resource failures (machine breakdowns), an arrival peak. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; apply: Name of the module to add (shifts, failures, arrival_peak); omit to list the verified candidates.; params: Optional parameters of the module, e.g. {"mtbf": 200}.

study_animation.summary: Make an animated GIF of one replication of a version (the step's stored seed): boxes shaded by utilisation, queue counts and a clock.
study_animation.doc: study_animation: Make an animated GIF of one replication of a version (the step's stored seed): boxes shaded by utilisation, queue counts and a clock. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; version: Version id, e.g. v002; omit for the last.; scenario: Name of a scenario of the model to animate instead of the baseline.

study_writeup.summary: Write a paper-style report of the study on request (STRESS-aligned sections: abstract, objective, model logic, data and assumptions, experimentation, verification and validation, results, limitations, discussion, references), built from the study folder.
study_writeup.doc: study_writeup: Write a paper-style report of the study on request (STRESS-aligned sections: abstract, objective, model logic, data and assumptions, experimentation, verification and validation, results, limitations, discussion, references), built from the study folder. Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).; discussion: Your own discussion text for section 8 (plain text, escaped in the page); omit for none.

study_slides.summary: Make a slide deck of the study on request: one HTML file, 16:9 slides (title and question, the answer, options compared, goals, model, assumptions, validation and precision, sensitivity when it was run, next steps).
study_slides.doc: study_slides: Make a slide deck of the study on request: one HTML file, 16:9 slides (title and question, the answer, options compared, goals, model, assumptions, validation and precision, sensitivity when it was run, next steps). Arguments: study: Study folder relative to the workspace root (the id study_start returned).

find_tool.summary: Find the tools that fit what you want to do, by a few words or a tool name you guessed ("validate against a formula", "make slides", "run_study").
find_tool.doc: find_tool: Find the tools that fit what you want to do, by a few words or a tool name you guessed ("validate against a formula", "make slides", "run_study"). Arguments: query:; limit:
